newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close at five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close at five-year high.

text.p: Argentine stocks shrugged off a Wall Street pullback and overcame technical resistance Wednesday, climbing to a five-year high at the close in brisk trading, analysts said.
"The market is rising thanks to stronger investment flows for medium and long-term portfolios -- it's no longer a dealer-driven market," said analyst Rodrigo Diz at brokers Velox Inversiones.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV posted its eighth consecutive gain and rose 1.4 percent to 764.71, its highest level since June 1992.
The bolsa had climbed 4.2 percent in the previous seven sessions.

"Investors were already upbeat before the U.S. Federal Reserve met yesterday to discuss rates, but most of them stayed on the sidelines, just in case rates were raised and the markets slumped," another trader said. "Now although rates stayed flat we've seen some profit-taking in New York, but the bolsa stayed firm and players were back in force."
Floor volume swelled to 31.6 million pesos from 19.5 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover rose to 114.8 million from 67.7 million Tuesday.
A stock exchange seat was sold by brokers Canton y Cia to De Ganai y Quirno for 530,000 pesos, up six percent from the price fetched at the previous auction Tuesday.
The broad market closed up 1.1 percent, with risers smashing decliners 52 to 13 and 16 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier gainers were holding company Comercial del Plata, which surged 5.5 percent, and carmaker Ciadea, construction stock Polledo and oil concern Astra, which rallied 4.1 percent, 3.7 percent and 3.6 percent, respectively.

The only MerVal losers were electricity generator Central Puerto, gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which shed 1.0 percent, 0.8 percent and 0.2 percent, respectively.
